free_tier.stated: Zero free bytes by design. ClearML's free tier is 'Flexible Storage. Store your datasets on any storage service and connect to ClearML – HTTP/S3/GCS/Azure/NAS'. That is bring-your-own-bucket: ClearML supplies the versioning layer, you supply (and pay for) the bytes. Differential storage reduces what you must store, but it does not create storage.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Yours, because the bytes are on your storage. ClearML itself charges nothing for egress since it never holds the data.

tooling: clearml Python SDK + clearml-agent; `Dataset.create()` / `dataset.add_files()` / `dataset.upload()` against any S3/GCS/Azure/HTTP/NAS backend. Mature and well documented.
chaining: There is nothing to multiply. The storage is a pre-existing account at AWS/GCS/Azure, all of which are excluded on cost grounds.
limits_note: Differential/dedup versioning means versions store only the change set from the parent, which is a genuine byte-saver. Free plan feature-limited (SSO and configuration vault are paid/enterprise). No included storage at all.
reliability_note: Reliable; the server is open source and self-hostable. But as a free-storage route it is a null result: it is a control plane, not a data plane.

extras.agent_focus: New and up-and-coming competitors to Hugging Face and ModelScope, judged on the hard test the brief sets: a credible HF competitor must permit multi-TB objects and generous per-account storage, because model weights and datasets routinely run to hundreds of GB / TiB. Split into three classes — Chinese domestic hubs (HF is blocked there, so a separate ecosystem exists), Western MLOps artifact stores (W&B/Comet/ClearML/Lightning/Deep Lake), and dataset-publishing startups (Source Cooperative, Oxen, OpenDataLab). Excluded and not re-reported: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, Civitai, Ollama, Replicate, DagsHub, OpenML, fal.ai, Baseten, Modal.
